examples.question_text: A drip must deliver $1.8$ L of fluid over $5$ hours. The drip gives $10$ drops/mL. Find the required rate in drops per minute.
examples.solution_text:
The quantities are drops, volume and time. Convert $1.8$ L to $1800$ mL and $5$ hours to $300$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{drops}}{\text{time}} &= \frac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}}\times\frac{\text{volume}}{\text{time}}\\&=\frac{10\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\times\frac{1800\text{ mL}}{300\text{ min}}\\&=\frac{60\text{ drops}}{1\text{ min}}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A drip delivers $18$ drops/min and gives $12$ drops/mL. How long will it take to deliver $720$ mL? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
examples.solution_text:
The quantities are time, drops and volume. Let the delivery time be $x$ minutes.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{time}}{\text{volume}} &= \frac{\text{time}}{\text{drops}}\times\frac{\text{drops}}{\text{volume}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{720\text{ mL}} &= \frac{1\text{ min}}{18\text{ drops}}\times\frac{12\text{ drops}}{1\text{ mL}}\\\frac{x\text{ min}}{720\text{ mL}} &= \frac{2\text{ min}}{3\text{ mL}}\\x &= 720\times\frac{2}{3}\\&=480\end{align*}$
The time is $480$ minutes, or $8$ hours $0$ minutes.

examples.question_text: A coffee shop buys $4$ kg bags of beans for $\$48$ each. Each cup uses $15$ g of beans. What is the cost of beans per cup?
examples.solution_text:
The quantities are cost, mass of beans and cups. Convert $4$ kg to $4000$ g.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{cost}}{\text{cup}} &= \frac{\text{cost}}{\text{beans}}\times\frac{\text{beans}}{\text{cup}}\\&=\frac{\$48}{4000\text{ g}}\times\frac{15\text{ g}}{1\text{ cup}}\\&=\frac{\$0.18}{1\text{ cup}}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Tropical fish produce $10$ new fry every $2$ days per female fish. There are $6$ female fish. At this rate, how long will it take to produce $105$ new fry?
examples.solution_text:
First find the daily rate for one female fish, then for all six.
$\begin{align*}\text{Rate per fish} &= \frac{10\text{ fry}}{2\text{ days}}\\&=\frac{5\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}}\\\text{Rate for six fish} &= 6\times\frac{5\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}}\\&=\frac{30\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}}\end{align*}$
Let the time be $x$ days.
$\begin{align*}\frac{30\text{ fry}}{1\text{ day}} &= \frac{105\text{ fry}}{x\text{ days}}\\\frac{x\text{ days}}{105\text{ fry}} &= \frac{1\text{ day}}{30\text{ fry}}\\x &= \frac{105}{30}\\&=3.5\end{align*}$
It takes $3.5$ days.

examples.question_text: A $20$ kg bag of flour costs $\$30$. Each cake uses $180$ g of flour. What does the calculation $\frac{30}{20\,000}\times180$ find?
examples.solution_text:
Write the units to identify the result.
$\frac{\$30}{20\,000\text{ g}}\times\frac{180\text{ g}}{1\text{ cake}}$
Grams cancel, leaving dollars per cake. The calculation finds the cost of flour used in one cake.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\$30}{20\,000}\times180\\&=\$0.27\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A factory produces $30$ widgets every $5$ minutes. Each widget uses $20$ g of plastic. Plastic costs $\$4$ per kg. Find the plastic cost per hour.
examples.solution_text:
The quantities are widgets, time, mass of plastic and cost. Convert $5$ minutes to $\frac{5}{60}$ hour and $20$ g to $0.02$ kg.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\text{cost}}{\text{time}} &= \frac{\text{widgets}}{\text{time}}\times\frac{\text{plastic}}{\text{widget}}\times\frac{\text{cost}}{\text{plastic}}\\&=\frac{30\text{ widgets}}{(5/60)\text{ h}}\times\frac{0.02\text{ kg}}{1\text{ widget}}\times\frac{\$4}{1\text{ kg}}\\&=\frac{360\text{ widgets}}{1\text{ h}}\times\frac{0.02\text{ kg}}{1\text{ widget}}\times\frac{\$4}{1\text{ kg}}\\&=\frac{\$28.80}{1\text{ h}}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: 1.8 L = 1800 mL; 5 h = 300 min. The required rate is 10 × 1800 ÷ 300 = 60 drops/min.
Time per volume is (1/18) × 12 = 2/3 min/mL. Delivering 720 mL takes 720 × 2/3 = 480 minutes = 8 hours.
One female produces 10 ÷ 2 = 5 fry/day. Six produce 30 fry/day, so producing 105 fry takes 105 ÷ 30 = 3.5 days.
20 kg = 20000 g. Dollars per gram multiplied by grams per cake gives dollars per cake: (30 ÷ 20000) × 180 = $0.27.
30 widgets per 5 minutes gives 360 widgets/hour. Each uses 0.02 kg costing 0.02 × $4 = $0.08; hourly plastic cost is 360 × $0.08 = $28.80.
